independentSourceObservations: One shared ungridded frame; horizontal baseline and vertical axis, with small wedge/end marks and no numbered scale.
Three solid response curves rise from the baseline vicinity, reach a tall narrow, intermediate, and low broad peak, then fall to finite right tails.
A broken near-vertical guide traverses the peak region and meets the horizontal baseline.
R-shaped curve labels with small index marks and fine oblique leaders sit to the right. Their coarse association is highest/middle/lowest; exact original leader tips and joins are not certified.

The amplitude mark has a small m/M-like subscript; the baseline meeting has a rounded origin mark; the guide-foot frequency mark has a rounded subscript. Pixels do not establish their alphabet, case or O/0/o identity.
modernAdditionsAndAdaptations: Current amplitude and Angular frequency are English edition-derived axis names, not certified translations of original individual glyphs.
Resonance is an edition-derived word instead of the unresolved source frequency subscript; the source origin glyph is omitted rather than declared numeric zero.
Plain axes, perpendicular orientation and common qualitative resonance alignment are modern regularization; original wedge topology and exact freehand positions remain held.
Smooth curves are an unnumbered normalized series-current model, not traced source coordinates or new read-from-graph data.
R1 < R2 < R3 comes from the current prose. Nearby R1/R3 labels and the short unarrowed R2 callout are authored associations, not resolutions of source leaders.
independentModernObservations: At 640 px, all three solid curves share a baseline/frame and the same visible peak region. R1 is highest and narrowest; R2 is intermediate; R3 is lowest and broadest. Their descending branches remain ordered.
The dashed guide is visually distinct from the solid response curves. It is not a fourth response curve or a numerical tick scale.
R1 is near the top peak; the short R2 callout contacts the intermediate curve, not the outer R1 branch. R3 sits below the low curve and to the right of the thin guide, with clear space.
At actual 331 and 342 px, the labels and inequality are legible, the R2 callout remains distinguishable, and the repaired R3 label is not crossed by the guide.
No visible label clipping, incoherent overlap, blank/black rendering, added numerical values, answer annotations, Cyrillic/Chinese text or Soviet cultural decoration.

independentMath.scope: Current modern qualitative steady-state series-current model and its displayed curve associations only; not exact source transcription or numerical source coordinates.
independentMath.reasoning: With fixed voltage amplitude and ideal L/C, I = U / sqrt(R^2 + (omega L - 1/(omega C))^2). For positive R the denominator is minimized at reactance cancellation, giving a finite peak U/R at the same angular frequency. Increasing R lowers the peak and broadens the relative resonance response. This is exactly the current-amplitude quantity identified by the edition.

independentSourceObservations: An antenna-like head joins the left winding above; a descending lead terminates at shrinking ground bars below.
A separate facing winding is at the left side of the right-hand tuned loop. There is visible space between the two windings, not an electrical connecting wire.
Top and bottom rails connect the right winding to two separated capacitor plates on the right side.
Two dark junction dots on the upper/lower rails each branch to an open rightward tap; the tap ends are not joined to a depicted receiver.
A dark diagonal shaft/tip-like mark crosses the capacitor region toward the upper right. Its exact endpoints, overlaps and electrical meaning are not established.
No readable source words or component values. Antenna-head detail and exact source winding turns are not certified counts.

independentModernObservations: At 640 px, both windings are continuous and face each other with a clear gap; the left antenna/ground branch is not electrically shorted to the right loop.
The upper and lower right-loop rails connect to the winding and respective capacitor stems. Two parallel capacitor plates retain a visible dielectric gap, with no connecting stroke across it.
Both rail dots visibly own their tap branches. The two rightward tap ends remain open and separate; no extra detector, load or ground connection is introduced.
At 331 and 342 px, both coils, both junctions, the capacitor gap and all five English labels remain legible/distinguishable. The longest label fits and does not cover a wire or another label.

independentMath.scope: Shown regularized circuit geometry and qualitative inductive-coupling/tuning meaning only; not a complete receiver netlist, original arrow meaning or source winding counts.
independentMath.reasoning: Separate coil windings allow inductive coupling without a direct electrical wire. The right coil and capacitor share the two loop nodes, and the open taps attach to those nodes rather than shorting the capacitor. Changing C at fixed L changes the ideal resonance frequency 1/sqrt(LC), matching the prose-supported adjustment label. No visual claim of perfect off-resonance rejection is added.
